subject: Function-address-identifier
notes: 'When function-prototype-name-1 is specified, the function-address-identifier has the characteristics of a function-pointer restricted to function-prototype-name-1.' The rule's whole observable consequence is that the sender then enters 14.9.39.3 SR20's same-signature compare as a restricted function-pointer, and that is exactly how it is implemented: the prototype arm of BindSetFunctionAddress runs the SAME PrototypeSignatures.Same test the pointer-to-pointer arm runs, against the receiver's own prototype, and COBOL1959 names the mismatch. It is ALSO why the prototype arm needs no run-time GR14 screen of its own - the characteristics are known at bind - while the identifier-1 arm does.
